---- Appellant  Versus   State of Chhattisgarh Through - Station House Officer, Police Station -  Kansabel, Distt.- Jashpur (C.G.)
 ----Respondent (Cause-title taken from Case Information System) For Appellant - Mr. Manoj Chouhan, Advocate.
For State/Respondent - Mr. Jitendra Shrivastava, Govt. Advocate.

Hon'ble Shri Justice Ravindra Kumar Agrawal Order on Board 10-06-2024 1. The instant criminal appeal is preferred under Section 14(A)(2) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (in short, 'the Act, 1989') against order dated 25-04-2024 passed by the learned Special Judge Atrocities Act, Jashpur (C.G.) (in bail application No.53/2024) whereby the application filed by the appellant under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. in connection with Crime No.13/2024 registered at Police Station Kansabel, District Jashpur (C.G.) for offence punishable under Sections 450, 376, 313, 34 of the IPC and Section 3(1)(2-V), 3(1)(b-1) of the Act, 1989, has been rejected.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. The facts of the case, in brief, are that on 18-10-2023 at about 10:00 a.m. accused Shyam Yadav has committed rape upon the prosecutrix on the pretext of marriage when she was alone in her house.
By the act of accused Shyam Yadav the prosecutrix conceived pregnancy for which on 08-02-2024 the accused administered pills by which she got aborted and thrown the fetus.
The incident was informed by her to her brother.
On 10-02-2024 when she was feeling illness the complainant taken her to the hospital and has got her admitted and lodged the report.
The FIR has been registered for the offence under Section 450, 376 and 313 of the IPC against accused Shyam Yadav.

During course of the investigation the memorandum statement of accused Shyam Yadav has been recorded on 11-02-2024 in which he disclosed that he purchased the pills (tablet) from Vaishali Medical Store which he got administered to the prosecutrix.
Thereafter, being owner of the shop of Vaishali Medical Store the appellant is apprehended his arrest in the above offence.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the appellant has been falsely implicated in the offence.

The only allegation against the present appellant is that the main accused Shyam Yadav Najre Imam vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142036866/
1 has purchased the tablet from the shop of the present appellant which is allegedly caused abortion of the prosecutrix.

entities.text: Shyam Yadav Najre Imam vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He would further submit that the police has verified the stock and purchase/sale bills of the medical shop of the appellant, but nothing adverse have been found by the police and it is only the memorandum of the accused available with the police to implicate the appellant in the offence.
The appellant is having a good reputation in the locality as well as in the community.
There is no evidence that in fact the main accused Shyam Yadav has purchased the tablet from the medical shop of the appellant.
The offence as alleged under Section 3(1)(2-V) and 3(1)(b-1) of the Act, 1989 is not attracted against the present appellant.

Therefore, the provision under Section 18 of the Act,
1989 would not be attracted.

He would further submit that merely mentioning of offence under the Act, 1989 in the case would not be sufficient to dislodge the appellant to take benefit of anticipatory bail under the provisions of Section 438 of the Cr.P.C.
There should be prima facie material available to show that the appellant has committed the offence as mentioned under the Act, 1989.

He would also submit that the allegation under the provisions of the Act, 1989, if at all, would be attracted against the co-accused Shyam Yadav only, therefore, the appeal be allowed and the appellant may be extended benefit of anticipatory bail.
4.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the submission made by learned counsel for the appellant and would submit that the FIR has been registered for offence under Section 450,
376 and 313 of the IPC.
However, during pendency of the investigation, offence under the Act, 1989 is also added.
He has read over the contents of the FIR in support of his contention.

He would further submit that the appellant is also responsible for offence under Section 313 of the IPC as he sold the tablet/pills to main accused Shyam Yadav which caused abortion of the prosecutirx.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

6. True it is that when the offence as alleged against any person by a person belonging to Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe community attracting the provisions of the Act, 1989 application for grant of anticipatory bail is not to be entertained.

However, there is no absolute bar in considering the application for grant of anticipatory bail, if the applicant succeeds to make out a case that after taking into consideration the entire allegation as reflected in the FIR the provisions of the Act, 1989 would not be attracted.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Prithvi Raj Chouhan Vs. Union of India and others, reported in (2020) 4 SCC 727 has observed in paras 11, 32 and 33 as under:-
"11.

entities.text: Prithvi Raj Chouhan Vs. Union of India and others, reported in (2020) 4 SCC 727
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Concerning the applicability of provisions of Section 438 CrPC, it shall not apply to the cases under the 1989 Act.
However, if the complaint does not make out a prima facie case for applicability of the provisions of the 1989 Act, the bar created by Section 18 and 18-A(i) shall not apply.
We have clarified this aspect while deciding the review petitions.

32. As far as the provision of Section 18-A and anticipatory bail is concerned, the judgment of Mishra, J. has stated that in cases where no prima facie materials exist warranting arrest in a complaint, the court has the inherent power to direct a pre-arrest bail.

2 33.

entities.text: Najre Imam vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
I would only add a caveat with the observation and emphasis that while considering any application seeking pre-arrest bail, the High Court has to balance the two interests; i.e. that the power is not so used as to convert the jurisdiction into that under Section 438 of the Criminal Procedure Code, but that it is used sparingly and such orders made in very exceptional cases where no prima facie offence is made out as shown in the FIR, and further also that if such orders are not made in those cases,
the result would inevitably be a miscarriage of justice or abuse of process of law.

I consider such stringent terms, otherwise contrary to the philosophy of bail,
absolutely essential, because a liberal use of the power to grant pre-arrest bail would defeat the intention of Parliament."
7. The contents of the FIR only mentioned that the main accused Shyam Yadav has administered pills to the prosecutrix by which she has got aborted.

The only evidence available against the present appellant is the memorandum of the co-accused who disclosed in his memorandum that he purchased the tablet or pills from Vaishali Medical Store, but physical verification of the stock and sale purchase bill, the police has not found any adverse material which connects the appellant with the offence in question that he sold the pills to the main accused Shyam Yadav.
There is no allegation against the present appellant that he committed rape upon the prosecutrix or involved in the said offence in any manner.

In view of the aforementioned facts of the case and allegation in the FIR made by the complainant, in the opinion of this Court offence under Section 3(1)(2-V) and 3(1)(b-1) of the Act, 1989 would not be attracted against the present appellant and therefore, it will fall within the exceptional cases.

8. Consequently, the appeal filed by the appellant is allowed and the impugned order passed by 25-04-2024 passed by the learned Special Judge Atrocities Act, Jashpur (C.G.) in bail application No.53/2024 is set aside.

It is directed that in the event of arrest of the applicant in connection with the aforesaid offence, he shall be released on bail by the officer arresting him on his furnishing a personal bond in sum of Rs.25,000/- with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the concerned Arresting Officer.
